headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage: cognee handles personal/finance/support data while RisingWave is a data engine with no documented isolation or retention controls in the pair.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, so direct prompt injection is not evidenced. However, cognee can ingest documents and session memory, and RisingWave is a data-engineering system that could plausibly sit in a pipeline if manually connected. The pathway is therefore only low-risk and requires unusual integration.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies RisingWave output into cognee inputs
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the two agents
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable any manual copy-paste bridge for untrusted content
Add a provenance label to all inter-agent payloads
requires-engineering: insert a sanitizer/formatter between pipeline stages

B_data_leakage.rationale: cognee explicitly touches personal data, finance data, support history, and documents, while RisingWave is a data-engineering system with no documented retention or isolation controls in this pair. The interaction could move sensitive data into outputs or logs in default pipeline use, so the blast radius includes multiple sensitive work products.
conditions: IF sensitive customer data is routed through RisingWave before reaching cognee
IF either agent logs or forwards payloads outside the intended tenant boundary
mitigations: Restrict test data to synthetic records
Verify both agents run in separate tenants
Turn off verbose logging for shared payloads
Review outbound destinations for both agents
requires-engineering: add field-level redaction before transfer

C_capability_conflict.rationale: cognee supports multiple instances with session memory, but RisingWave exposes no write or OAuth scopes here, so overlapping mutable-resource conflict is not documented. The pair only shows a plausible conflict if an operator wires both to the same external store or directory, making this an unusual-configuration issue.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same external directory or database
IF an orchestrator gives them shared mutable credentials
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories
Use separate service accounts
Avoid concurrent writes to the same dataset
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: cognee produces decisions, workflows, and successful implementations, which RisingWave could consume if chained as a downstream data system. Because RisingWave has no documented verification step in the profile, A's output could be treated as authoritative by B in a default pipeline, creating a plausible cascading-error path.
conditions: IF RisingWave ingests cognee-generated records without validation
IF downstream jobs act on those records as ground truth
mitigations: Add schema validation before ingestion
Require human review for high-impact records
Tag cognee outputs as untrusted until checked
Compare outputs against a second source
requires-engineering: implement verification gates in the pipeline

E_compliance.rationale: cognee touches personal data, finance data, and support history, while RisingWave has no documented residency, retention, or subject-rights controls in the profile. That mismatch can create compliance gaps when regulated data is processed through the pair, even though the exact jurisdictional breach is not specified.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is processed through both agents
IF retention or deletion requests must propagate across the pair
mitigations: Map each data class to an approved processing path
Confirm retention settings for both systems
Exclude regulated records from noncompliant flows
Document deletion/export handling end to end
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention
